$comment: Single source of truth for error codes. Run `yarn errors:generate` after editing; CI runs `yarn errors:check`.

codes.description: The native module is not registered in this build.
codes.troubleshooting: Rebuild the app after installing or upgrading the package. Expo Go is not supported; use a development build.

codes.description: The current platform or OS release cannot perform the operation.
codes.troubleshooting: Check `getCapabilities()` before calling platform-specific APIs. iOS has no discovery, pairing, server sockets or adapter state.

codes.description: An argument or option is missing, unknown, of the wrong type or out of range.
codes.troubleshooting: The message names the offending argument or option key. Option keys are camelCase; v1 keys such as `DELIMITER` are rejected.

codes.description: The device has no Bluetooth hardware.
codes.troubleshooting: Hide Bluetooth features on this device.

codes.description: Bluetooth is switched off.
codes.troubleshooting: Ask the user to turn Bluetooth on, for example with `requestEnable()` on Android.

codes.description: A runtime permission required by the operation is not granted.
codes.troubleshooting: `missingPermissions` lists what is missing. Call `requestPermissions(scope)` first.

codes.description: Android 7-11 (API 24-30) only returns discovery results while Location Services is switched on.
codes.troubleshooting: Ask the user to switch on Location Services, then retry discovery.

codes.description: The user declined a system prompt or dismissed a picker.
codes.troubleshooting: Explain why the action is needed before asking again.

codes.description: No Android activity is in the foreground to show a system prompt or screen.
codes.troubleshooting: Call the API while the app is in the foreground.

codes.description: An unexpected failure with no specific mapping.
codes.troubleshooting: Inspect `nativeCode` and `nativeMessage`, and report the issue with debug logs.

codes.description: The requested device or accessory could not be found.
codes.troubleshooting: Make sure the device is powered on, in range and discoverable.

codes.description: A discovery session started by the library is already running.
codes.troubleshooting: Wait for the running session to finish, or call `cancelDiscovery()`.

codes.description: The OS refused to start discovery.
codes.troubleshooting: Retry after a short delay; check `nativeMessage` for the OS reason.

codes.description: A pairing started by the library for the same device is still pending.
codes.troubleshooting: Await the pending `pair()` call.

codes.description: Bonding ended without a bond, or the OS refused to start bonding.
codes.troubleshooting: The user may have declined or entered a wrong PIN. Retry, or pair from system settings.

codes.description: Bonding did not finish within the timeout.
codes.troubleshooting: Increase `timeoutMs` or retry with the device closer.

codes.description: The connection attempt failed.
codes.troubleshooting: `nativeMessage` carries the OS reason. On Android, try `android.transport: 'insecure'` or `android.fallbackChannel`.

codes.description: The connection attempt did not complete within the timeout.
codes.troubleshooting: Make sure the device is in range and accepts connections, or increase `timeoutMs`.

codes.description: The connection attempt was cancelled through its abort signal.
codes.troubleshooting: No action needed.

codes.description: A connection to the same target already exists.
codes.troubleshooting: Use `getConnection(error.connectionId)` to reuse the existing connection.

codes.description: A connection attempt to the same target is already pending.
codes.troubleshooting: Await the pending `connect()` call.

codes.description: The connection has already ended.
codes.troubleshooting: Connect again before writing.

codes.description: The connection ended because of an unexpected local failure.
codes.troubleshooting: Reconnect; inspect `nativeMessage` if it keeps happening.

codes.description: Listening for incoming connections failed.
codes.troubleshooting: Check `nativeMessage`; another app may be listening on the same service.

codes.description: No device connected within the accept timeout.
codes.troubleshooting: Call `accept()` again, or increase `timeoutMs`.

codes.description: The pending accept was cancelled.
codes.troubleshooting: No action needed.

codes.description: Another accept is already pending.
codes.troubleshooting: Await the pending `accept()` or call `cancelAccept()`.

codes.description: The OS reported an error while writing; the connection has ended.
codes.troubleshooting: Reconnect and resend.

codes.description: A write was not fully accepted within its timeout; the connection has ended.
codes.troubleshooting: The remote device stopped reading. Reconnect and resend.

codes.description: No frame arrived within the read timeout.
codes.troubleshooting: The connection stays open; retry the read or resend the request.

codes.description: Received data exceeded the configured buffer limit.
codes.troubleshooting: Attach a data listener or reader sooner, or raise `maxBufferBytes` / `maxFrameBytes`.

codes.description: The protocol is not listed in UISupportedExternalAccessoryProtocols.
codes.troubleshooting: Add the protocol to Info.plist (or the config plugin's `protocols` option) and rebuild.

codes.description: The accessory does not support the requested protocol.
codes.troubleshooting: Use one of the accessory's `protocolStrings`.

codes.description: The accessory is not currently connected to the OS.
codes.troubleshooting: Accessory ids change on every reconnect; call `getConnectedAccessories()` again.

codes.description: The OS refused to open a session with the accessory.
codes.troubleshooting: Another app may hold the session, or the accessory rejected it. Check `nativeMessage`.
